title: Hybridization Involving s and p Orbitals
notes: **Hybridization:** the concept that atomic orbitals of similar energy mix to form new equivalent orbitals called hybrid orbitals, which then overlap to form bonds.
**sp hybridization:** one s + one p gives two sp orbitals, linear geometry, 180Â° bond angle. Example: $BeCl_2$, $CO_2$.
**sp$^2$ hybridization:** one s + two p gives three sp$^2$ orbitals, trigonal planar geometry, 120Â° bond angle. Example: $BF_3$, $C_2H_4$ (double bond contains one $\sigma$ and one $\pi$).
**sp$^3$ hybridization:** one s + three p gives four sp$^3$ orbitals, tetrahedral geometry, 109.5Â° bond angle. Example: $CH_4$, $C_2H_6$.
**Why hybridize:** VBT explains molecular geometry better than pure atomic orbital overlap. The hybrid orbitals point in directions that minimize electron-pair repulsion.
